DILG BAGONG PILIPINAS Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City wmv.diG.gov.ph O!'-G OPINION NO. SEP 11 FAUSTO P. TAN Sangguniang Bayan Secretary Municipality of Don Marcelino Province of Davao Occidental faustotan.donmarcelino@gmail.com Dear Mr. Tan: This has reference to your letter dated 8 April 2024 seeking this Department's legal opinion on the following queries: 1. 2. 3. 4. Whether the power to call for a special session and the power to certify a certain measure as urgent are conferred to the mayor or to the majority of the Sanggunian Bayan Members, or both; If the answer in the first query is in the affirmative, can it be safely inferred that without the letter request of the Mayor for the Sangguniang Bayan to certify the measure as urgent, the latter has no justifiable basis to consider the matter as urgent for their immediate deliberation? Can the Sanggunian be obligated to seek the letter request of the former to certify a certain measure as urgent for it to be immediately deliberated upon by the latter in the plenary session? Can the Sanggunian validly exercise its implied power, during a regular session, to decide through the majority votes to certify the urgency of a proposed measure? Considering the first and second queries are interrelated, we will answer said queries in one discussion. At the onset, Section 52 (b) of R.A. 7160, otherwise known as the Local Government Code (LGC) is instructive regarding who has the power to call for a special session, viz: Section 52. Sessions. - xxx (b) When public interest so demands, special sessions may be called bv the local chief executive or by a majority of the members of the sanqgunian. "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

[Emphasis and underlining supplied]. As to the power to certify a certain measure as urgent, please be informed that Article 107 of the Implementing Rules and Regulations of the LGC recognizes the power of the local chief executive (LCE) to determine the matters to be considered urgent, thus: "ARTICLE 107. Ordinances and Resolution. — The following rules shall govern the enactment of ordinances and resolutions: Xxxx (e) Any legislative matter duly certified by the local chief executive as urgent, whether or not it is included in the calendar of business, may be presented and considered by the body at the same meeting without need of suspending the rules." From the foregoing, the LGC specifically provides that special sessions may be called by the local chief executive by a majority of the members of the sanggunian. The LCE is likewise vested with an authority to certify as urgent any legislative matter to respond quickly to any exigency of public service, public emergency, or calamity which requires immediate action and solution. 1 Thus, the Sanngguniang Bayan lacks the authority to certify as urgent any legislative item pending with them for deliberate action, as such authority is reserved for the LCE. As to the third query and fourth query, we will likewise discuss in one discussion. Please be informed, there is nothing in the LGC that prohibits the Sanggunian to request from the LCE to certify a certain measure as urgent. However, it is within the discretion and authority of the LCE whether to certify as urgent any legislative matter as discussed above. The Sanggunian cannot compel the LCE to declare a certain measure as urgent. Per the aforequoted Article 107 of the IRR of the LGC, it is the LCE who is vested with the authority to certify as urgent any legislative measure with the authority to certify as urgent any legislative matters which require immediate attention and solution. Such authority is based on the duty of the LCE to determine the programs, projects or activities of the LGU, including the priority thrust of his administration. Accordingly, we are of the opinion that the authority of the LCE to certify as urgent any legislative matter is granted by law in order to allow LGUs, at the instance of the LCE, to respond quickly, through legislative measures, any exigency of public service, public emergency, or calamity which requires immediate attention and solution. Therefore, the authority to certify as urgent any legislative measure is attached to the position of the LCE.2 Thus, the Sangguniang may not validly exercise its implied power, during a regular session, to decide through the majority votes to certify the urgency of a proposed measure as said authority is vested with the LCE. DILG Opinion No. 103 s. 2021, August 9, 2021 2 Ibid Page 2 of 3

The opinion of this Department is based solely on the facts and representations you have narrated in your letter and our appreciation of the same. We hope to have addressed your concern accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, B THORITY OF THE SECRETARY: AN IC R R. LLAMAS nd s retary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs OUS L JVRULLLS-LRALLDnasm Page 3 of 3
